newsitem.title: USA: U.S., Japan, South Korea hold policy meeting.
newsitem.headline: U.S., Japan, South Korea hold policy meeting.

text.p: Officials from the United States, Japan and South Korea held a "brainstorming" session on Saturday on their policy toward North Korea, discussing many sensitive issues, a South Korea spokesman said.
The meeting came in the wake of rare bilateral talks on Friday between the United States and North Korea, the highest level official talks between the two nations in more than a year.

On Saturday, such sensitive issues as high-level defections from the North and reports of food shortages in the isolationist Communist nation were discussed. The three-way talks concerned policy cooperation among the United States, Japan and South Korea toward North Korea, which a spokesman for South Korea's Mission to the United Nations, Ji Won Suh, described as "successful."
"Because of some turbulent days considered to be ahead for North Korea, further keen observation on the situation in North Korea will be worthwhile," Suh said.

The meetings were taking place during a tense period on the Korean peninsula following a string of defections from the North and reports of famine and economic collapse in the hardline Communist state.

The three nations discussed last month's defection of 74-year-old ideologue Hwang Jang-yop, ranked 24th in Pyongyang's hierarchy, Suh said, adding that a "careful watch for further developments" was "desirable."
The United States was expected to donate $10 million worth of grain and South Korea was to donate $6 million in food to North Korea to aid in the food shortage, he said.
Suh said the meeting, which ended about midday, was a "brainstorming" session, and added, "no decisive conclusion of what is good or not was made."

At Friday's wide-ranging talks between the United States and North Korea, which lasted almost 11 hours, the two countries agreed to work on three major bilateral issues -- nonproliferation of missiles, the recovery of remains of missing U.S. servicemen from the Korean War and the establishment of liaison offices in each country.

The most significant of the meetings and briefings this past week in New York involving the United States, North Korea and South Korea was on Wednesday, when U.S. and South Korean officials briefed North Korea on details of proposed four-way talks, which would include China, to forge a new agreement to replace the armistice that ended the 1950-53 Korean War.
That meeting aroused new hopes that the isolationist Communist nation would join in peace talks with South Korea.
At Saturday's meeting, Japanese officials expressed their support for the proposed four-way talks, the South Korean spokesman said.
Japan, South Korea and the United States agreed to continue to hold discussions, but no dates were set, he said.
